standard_prerequisites.name: The length formula for a flat local homomorphism
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Algebra, label algebra-lemma-pullback-module, invoked at proof line 2623
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the equality between the order at the base of a rational function times the length of the source local ring over the expanded maximal ideal and the order of the function upstairs, which is the coefficient identity.

core_obligations: Reduce to a coefficient comparison: since the morphism is flat it is dominant, so the function may be viewed upstairs; fix an integral closed subscheme of the source of the relevant dimension with generic point xi and observe that if the closure of its image has dimension greater than n - 1 then both coefficients vanish (proof lines 2602-2611).

Pass to local algebra: assume the closure of the image is an integral closed subscheme of dimension n - 1 with generic point the image of xi, and set up the two local rings at these generic points, which form a flat local homomorphism of Noetherian local domains of dimension one (proof lines 2611-2617).

Compare the coefficients: the coefficient in the pulled back divisor is the order at the base times the length of the source over the expanded maximal ideal, while the coefficient on the other side is the order of the function upstairs, and the equality is the length formula for a flat local homomorphism, with the author omitting the details (proof lines 2618-2624).
proof_roadmap: Reduce to a coefficient comparison at a codimension one component (proof lines 2602-2611).
Set up the flat local homomorphism of one-dimensional local domains (proof lines 2611-2617).
difficulty_reason: The lemma computes the flat pullback of the divisor of a rational function on an integral scheme as the divisor of the same function on the source (statement lines 2589-2600, tag 02RU-adjacent). The proof reduces to a coefficient comparison at an integral closed subscheme of codimension one, passes to the two local rings at the generic points, which form a flat local homomorphism of one-dimensional Noetherian local domains, and identifies the two coefficients as an order times a length and an order, equal by the length formula for flat local maps. The reduction to the local statement is the substance, so the claim is H2.
